artboards.title: Option B — Out on the Field

annotations.text:
Three directions for the homepage, plus how each looks on a phone.

Anything in [square brackets] is a placeholder — event names, dates, venues and news titles all come live from Spanner, so I haven't invented any. Everything else is real club copy.

The photos are the club's own, pulled from the repo.

What's making it feel cluttered today:

• The page opens with an <h1> that just says "Home"
• Everything sits at one size on one white slab — no hierarchy to follow
• News posts render full-length, so one long one buries the rest
• The 2.5MB background photo is only visible as a 12px margin
• 6 nav links + a two-line wordmark + an 80px logo all crammed into 1024px

OPTION A — CLUB GREEN
The careful fix.

Same structure, same pages, same familiar feel — but with a real hero, a proper type ramp, and generous space. News is trimmed to excerpts so one long post can't take over.

Why: lowest risk. Nobody in the club has to relearn anything, and it's the quickest to build.

Tradeoff: safe. It solves the clutter but nothing about it will stop a stranger scrolling past.

OPTION B — OUT ON THE FIELD
Lead with the mud.

Full-bleed photo hero, big confident type, then the five disciplines shown as photos rather than described in paragraphs. Built to recruit.

Why: the club's best asset is what it looks like on a wet Sunday, and right now the site hides that behind a white box.

Tradeoff: it lives or dies on the photography — someone has to keep feeding it good pictures. Heaviest page of the three, and a member wanting to book scrolls past the hero to get there.

OPTION C — NOTICEBOARD
What's on, can I book.

No hero at all. The events board IS the homepage, grouped by month with clear booking states, and everything else moves to a sidebar. The whole thing fits on one screen.

Why: for the hundred-plus existing members, this is the only question the site ever has to answer.

Tradeoff: coldest of the three to a newcomer, and it looks empty in the quiet months when there's nothing in the calendar.
Phone views — worth weighing these heavily. Most people will meet this site on a phone, and the current one squeezes a 5em logo and a two-line wordmark into 390px before you reach any content.
